clippings.speaker: Christopher Nolan
clippings.quote: I wrote out a page of what I considered to be the heart of the story—the relationships, the idea of a father having to leave his children … I gave it to Hans and said, ‘Work on that for a day and give me what you’ve got at the end of the day, and that’ll be the seed from which we can grow the score.’
clippings.title: The Iris Interview: Christopher Nolan, Jonathan Nolan and Emma Thomas talk about working on Interstellar
clippings.context: Nolan's own account of the one-page letter he gave Zimmer before writing the script, in a Q&A with Jonathan Nolan and Emma Thomas.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: I played him this thing, and it’s tiny, a musical love letter to my son. And I said to him, “What do you think?” And he paused for a second, and said, “I’d better make the movie now.”
clippings.title: OscarWrap: Christopher Nolan and ‘Interstellar’ Dream Team Talk Sound, Edit, Design
clippings.context: Zimmer, interviewed by Steve Pond for TheWrap's awards issue, describes playing Nolan the piece he wrote in a day from the one-page letter.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: Well it’s really simple. The answer is Chris Nolan and the way we work together. We get breathless with throwing ideas at each other and we cross all the lines. It’s like Chris will be talking about music and I’ll be talking about story.
clippings.title: Hans Zimmer Talks About Scoring Interstellar, and Why Batman Needs a New Theme
clippings.context: Interview with Don Kaye; Zimmer answering why he writes such good scores for Nolan, right after describing Nolan as 'part of the band' in his studio.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Nolan
clippings.quote: What I decided to do was give it to Hans and let him run with it and see if in some way it might inform elements of the score
clippings.title: INCEPTION Interview Leonardo DiCaprio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, Marion Cotillard, Tom Hardy, Ken Watanabe, Christopher Nolan, Hans Zimmer
clippings.context: Inception press conference transcript; Nolan on handing Zimmer the Edith Piaf song from the script so it could shape the score.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: In a funny way, what I think we did do was a sort of shared dreaming thing, and we did prove it’s possible, because when I finally saw the film, and when Chris had laid in all my music, I was actually surprised how well these two worlds existed together.
clippings.title: INCEPTION Interview Leonardo DiCaprio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Ellen Page, Marion Cotillard, Tom Hardy, Ken Watanabe, Christopher Nolan, Hans Zimmer
clippings.context: Same press conference; Zimmer explains that Nolan would not show him footage until he had written the music.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Nolan
clippings.quote: I asked Hans not to write any emotional music. What I said to him was I wanted objectivity — the way I wanted to make the film was, it’s all about suspense and tension and not at all about emotion.
clippings.publication: Gulf News (New York Times News Service)
clippings.title: ‘Dunkirk’ soundtrack: How it all came together
clippings.context: Melena Ryzik's New York Times piece on the Dunkirk score (July 2017), syndicated openly by Gulf News; Nolan spoke separately from Vietnam during the press tour.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Nolan
clippings.quote: I didn’t really say this to Hans, but it played at my father’s funeral a few years ago. I just find it unbearably moving.
clippings.publication: Gulf News (New York Times News Service)
clippings.title: ‘Dunkirk’ soundtrack: How it all came together
clippings.context: Nolan on why he suggested Elgar's 'Nimrod' for the Dunkirk score, which Zimmer then slowed and reworked.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: This was the closest collaboration that I ever had with a director where even though he would never ever play a note, he somehow played every note that was in that score.
clippings.publication: Gulf News (New York Times News Service)
clippings.title: ‘Dunkirk’ soundtrack: How it all came together
clippings.context: Zimmer to the New York Times on Dunkirk; in the same piece he adds, 'Can I say something rude? This score is Chris Nolan’s score.'

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: Chris [Nolan] understands I have to do it. He’s going to be just fine. Ludwig and I are friends. Forget the friend part, he’s really good.
clippings.title: Here’s why Hans Zimmer isn’t working on Christopher Nolan’s next film
clippings.context: Zimmer explaining why he chose Dune over Tenet, which went to Ludwig Göransson; originally said on The Playlist's podcast, which Yahoo does not credit by name.

clippings.speaker: Hans Zimmer
clippings.quote: Not great. … So Chris realized that, and he realized that that’s where my focus was at that moment.
clippings.title: How Christopher Nolan Reacted to Hans Zimmer Choosing Dune Over Tenet
clippings.context: Zimmer on CinemaBlend's ReelBlend podcast, asked how Nolan took the news; the elided middle explains that touring had pulled his focus toward Dune.

notes: Zimmer talking about Nolan was easy to find; Nolan's own words about Zimmer were much harder, because most coverage reaches Nolan only through Zimmer's retellings. WebFetch caps each quote it returns at about 125 characters, so longer excerpts were rebuilt from consecutive pieces, and every join was checked against the page for contiguity. Joins with an ellipsis mark material skipped on purpose. The source pages use curly quotes, and these were kept. Dead ends: the Classic FM Nolan interview ('We fight like cats and dogs but in the best, the most productive way', Andrew Collins, 18 July 2017) returns 404, and web.archive.org could not be fetched, so none of its quotes are included even though the headline came up in search. The CinemaBlend ReelBlend article (the original source of the 'Not great' quote) and the CinemaBlend Interstellar piece loaded without article body; Screen Rant was used instead, marked secondhand. The Playlist 2019 Dune/Tenet article (403) was the original source of 'Chris understands', so Yahoo UK was used, marked secondhand. Collider quotes the same remark in different wording ('I have to do it, and Chris understands I have to do it, and he’s gonna be just fine'). The Hollywood Reporter Dunkirk pieces redirect to a TollBit paywall and were skipped. PressReader copies (Columbus Dispatch, National Post) were skipped as a subscription aggregator. The NYT original (Melena Ryzik, July 2017) is paywalled, so the openly syndicated Gulf News reprint was used; its page date (2018-09-15) is a 'last updated' stamp, not the original publication date. The AP Dunkirk Q&A, where Nolan says he sent Hans a recording of his watch, could not be fetched (apnews.com blocked). No source was found with Nolan himself explaining why Zimmer did not score Tenet or Oppenheimer; only Zimmer's side of the split is covered. Unused but verified extras: Grantland 2014 (Matt Patches) has Zimmer: 'The only way I can put it is he's in my band. I'm in his band'. Saturday Evening Post 2017 has Zimmer: 'I felt Chris’ hand on my hand like he was pressing the keys down with me.' Gulf News/NYT has Nolan: 'Hans didn’t use that crutch.' DGA Quarterly Summer 2017 has Nolan: 'And this extended to Hans' work, which had to obey these structures, too.' Far Out Magazine retells the Interstellar letter story from a Jonathan Ross interview (secondhand).
